Need answer q1: "How are the two range-level seeding assignments related within one retained EU?" Criteria options: both_seeded, complementary_assignment, conflicting, independent_assignments, not_stated, other, permanent_range.
Evidence: "Within an EU, seeding is randomly assigned to one range and not the other. The authors explicitly say the Medicine Bow assignment plot would have the opposite shading from the Sierra Madre plot." Scope: one EU includes paired ranges; target sites HY (Sierra Madre) and GL (Medicine Bow). This exactly complementary assignment: one joint allocation selects seeded range, other receives complementary unseeded assignment. So q1 = complementary_assignment.

q2: "Does an assigned-unseeded label, by itself, establish zero physical exposure to seeding material in this study?" Options: assignment_only; exposure_confirmed_everywhere; zero_exposure_established; not_stated; conflicting.
Evidence: assigned-unseeded label? Design assignment not physical exposure. CLOUD-2014 slide 24 ground-based ice nucleus indicates silver iodide reached Medicine Bow in 21 Sierra Madre seeding cases; slide 29 modeled enhanced precipitation. Scope says auxiliary gauges and possible cross-range contamination do not redefine assigned treatment. The question: Does assigned-unseeded label, by itself, establish zero physical exposure? It doesn't; establishes planned allocation, while physical exposure requires additional evidence because cross-range contamination discussed. This is option assignment_only. It says "No; it establishes the planned allocation..." So q2 = assignment_only. Need not_stated? Evidence explicitly discusses contamination and assignment does not equal exposure. It asks "by itself". Evidence: "target treatment assignment... possible cross-range contamination do not redefine assigned treatment" and ground measurements indicate cross contamination. So assignment_only is correct.

Need final JSON only. Ensure no calculation. Could there be conflicting due Table 1 sum 8 vs 9? Scope not about q1/q2. no.
